scope: Advance a local instruction slice instead of updating a numeric instruction index on every dispatch. Retain existing workspace register storage after measuring two alternative borrowed layouts. No bytecode, cache or allocation changes.

method.device: ESP32 rev3.1, 240MHz, one core, standalone profiling image, Wi-Fi off, GPIO untouched. Same workloads, parameters and 32 timestamps per case. CRC and serial output outside timed evaluation.
method.release: opt-level=3, fat LTO, one codegen unit, panic=abort, debug=2 for symbols. Timed device images have no per-instruction counters.
method.hotspots: Interrupted PCs at 997 and 1999 microseconds bracketed by two unsampled controls. Self-symbol percentages include inlined helpers. Estimated function times use sample share times warm control mean.
method.equivalence: All 19 prepared archives and the manifest are byte-for-byte identical in baseline, cursor and both register experiments. All 608 host CRCs and full instruction-signature counts match. Each device capture verifies 544 frames, all 17 cases and all 16 profiling/control windows.
method.limitations: Prepared evaluation and output-buffer encoding only. No network, storage, DMA or physical LED latency. Short windows do not establish full-show deadlines or maximum nested stack use. No new laptop timings.

register_findings: The original workspace embeds VmRegisters; optimized code keeps its base in a CPU register. Splitting it does not eliminate a pointer chase. Nine slices eagerly preload and spill bank pointers/lengths, grow the invocation object and run stack frames, and penalize short invocations. One register reference plus array/loop references reduces this overhead but does not outperform cursor-only playback. Keep the existing compact ownership structure. Exact shares attributable to register allocation versus code layout were not separately measured.
native_scope: Symbol sizes and Xtensa entry stack-frame operands from the exact profiling ELFs. Run frames exclude callers, callees and nested invocations. Cursor code retains checked slice rebasing at taken branches.

full_controller_build.configuration: release loader with dig-quad; built and linked, not flashed

memory.notes: Heap accounting excludes stack and native code. Existing workspace layout and capacities are unchanged.

recollection: Reflashed the accepted cursor ELF and recollected a complete report under access-cursor-confirmation. Its serial bytes exactly match the first capture; this is not counted as an independent statistical timing sample.
verification: cargo fmt, full pnpm check including firmware-owned host storage tests and Clippy, and release dig-quad loader build passed on the final cursor source. All 102 runtime unit tests passed. The board is left on the accepted standalone profiling image.
